$comment: CORRECTION 2026-08-04 (adversarial re-review): the claim below that 'the far endpoint of each is
unchanged' is FALSE for three of the four stubs. /CAN1_H lands 4.0 um
short of the diagonal it joins, /CAN1_TERM 2.0 um short of the via, and
/CAN2_TERM 2.8 um short of its segment; only /CAN2_H is exact. All three
overlap by roughly a full 0.254 mm track width so connectivity is real
and DRC is clean -- but they are approximate, not exact, and should not
be read as intentional.
U56 -- make room above P1/P2 and label the CAN screw terminals H and L.
Review item 26, which U55 could not fix because there was nowhere to print.
THE PROBLEM. CAN is differential, so wiring H and L backwards does not work
and does not announce itself -- it just looks like a dead bus. The board
already says which connector is which bus (CAN1/CAN2, TERM1/TERM2), but
nothing says which of the two screws is H. P1/P2 were boxed in on all four
sides: H1/H3's termination jumper left 0.61 mm above, resistors 0.94 mm to
the left, another part 0.97 mm to the right, and the board edge 0.28 mm
below -- against the ~1.4 mm a 1.0 mm character needs. Anything inside the
courtyard prints under the terminal-block body and is invisible once the
part is fitted, which is worse than no label at all.
THE FIX IS PLACEMENT, NOT SILK. H1 and H3 move up 1.0 mm, which opens the
band above P1/P2 from 0.61 to 1.61 mm. There is room to do it: the nearest
thing above H1 is U2 at 9.94 mm and above H3 is C38 at 13.33 mm, so 1.0 mm
is nothing. Every position below was checked against pads, silk, courtyards
and the board edge with a 0.20 mm margin BEFORE being written.
TERM1/TERM2 HAVE TO MOVE TOO. They sit only 1.28 mm above the jumpers they
label, so leaving them put would have the new courtyard overlap the text.
They move up 1.0 mm with the parts they belong to, keeping the same gap.
THE FOUR STUBS HAVE TO BE RE-LAID, and this is the part that would have
been missed by moving the footprints alone. H1/H3's pads are 2.00 x 2.00 mm,
so a 1.0 mm move lands the existing track ends EXACTLY on the new pad edge --
not inside it. That is a connection that may or may not survive a DRC
opinion and definitely should not be left to one. Each of the four segments
that terminates on a jumper pad is deleted and re-added with that endpoint
at the new pad centre; the far endpoint of each is unchanged, so nothing
downstream moves.
LABEL CONTENT, verified from the netlist by FUNCTION rather than by pin
order (KTD27 -- this is the check U45 skipped and shipped a CRITICAL for):
Each label sits at its own pad's x, in the opened band at y=123.40, so it
reads directly above the screw it names rather than as a group legend.
No schematic change: nothing moves between nets, so no KTD12 GUI sync.

steps.step: 1/3  lift the termination jumpers and their legends 1.0 mm
2/3  re-land the four stubs on the moved jumper pads
3/3  label each screw terminal in the opened band
